Make-believe field notes

Read a clue, imagine two ways it could have happened, and describe one more clue you would look for. You can think it through, tell the story aloud, or write it on paper.

Inspired by the historical activity “Mystical Creatures,” credited to @Schmoneybags (page 16). The scenes and creatures below were invented for this exercise. They are separate from real Safari wildlife, records and rewards.

A trail in the sand

Three small marks repeat beside the water. The marks stop where the sand gets wet. What do you know from the marks alone?

Read two possible stories

A make-believe reed skipper may have hopped along the dry bank. Or a loose twig may have caught and skipped across the sand. Look for the same repeating marks farther up the bank before picking a story.

A ring of leaves

Five leaves form a rough ring on a bench. Every leaf points inward. What could have put them there?

Read two possible stories

An imaginary leaf tailor may have laid them out for a pattern. Or someone may have arranged them while resting. Look for another pattern with the same number and direction of leaves.

Make your own field note

Start with one thing you could see, hear or feel. Give it two different explanations. End by naming a clue that would help you tell the explanations apart.
